meta.scope: Rental-income rules that apply to Property S (San Francisco, 94122, three units, two rented) and that would apply to Property C if it were rented after inheritance.
meta.privacy: Rent roll is stated as an aggregate monthly figure only. No tenant names, unit identifiers, tenancy start dates, or lease terms are stored.

rows.label: Allowable annual rent increase for rent-controlled units, effective 2026-03-01 through 2027-02-28
rows.source_name: City and County of San Francisco (sf.gov), Rent Board announcement dated 2026-01-14
rows.note: Calculated as 60% of the change in Bay Area CPI. The prior period (2025-03-01 to 2026-02-28) was 1.4%.

rows.label: Allowable annual rent increase for the prior period, 2025-03-01 through 2026-02-28
rows.source_name: City and County of San Francisco (sf.gov)
rows.note: Useful as a sense-check: recent San Francisco allowable increases have run roughly 1.4-1.7% a year.

rows.label: Which units the 1.6% cap covers
rows.note: Commonly described as buildings with a certificate of occupancy on or before 1979-06-13, with single-family homes and condos exempt under Costa-Hawkins. This session confirmed the 1.6% figure from an official source but did not retrieve the coverage rules from the San Francisco Rent Ordinance, so the field is left blank. Material: Property S is a three-unit building and its certificate-of-occupancy date determines whether the 1.6% cap or the AB 1482 cap governs.

rows.label: Statewide annual rent increase cap formula (Tenant Protection Act of 2019, AB 1482)
rows.value: 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower
rows.source_name: California Legislative Information, Civil Code section 1947.12(a)(1)
rows.note: Applies to the lowest gross rental rate charged in the prior 12 months. Also limits increases to two increments in any 12-month period. Civil Code 1947.12(d) exempts, among others, housing subject to a local ordinance that restricts annual increases to less than this amount, and housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years.

rows.label: Numeric AB 1482 cap currently in force for San Francisco
rows.note: The statute gives the formula, not the annual number. Deriving the number requires the official regional CPI figure for the period. Aggregator sites published an 8.8% figure for the San Francisco-Oakland-Hayward region, but that was not confirmed against a BLS release, so the field is left blank. Retrieve from BLS CPI-U data for the San Francisco-Oakland-Hayward metropolitan area.

rows.label: Current gross rent collected, two of three units
rows.note: Equivalent to 85,800 USD/yr. Owner states they can live at the property as a primary residence without losing rental income, which implies the third unit is the owner's unit and is not rented.

rows.label: Market rent achievable if the owner-occupied third unit were rented
rows.note: This is the pivot number for the 'move to Cupertino' scenario: moving into Property C frees the Property S unit for rent. No official source publishes rent for a specific unit, and no appraisal was obtained. Obtain three comparable rentals or a broker opinion before acting.

rows.label: Market rent achievable for Property C if rented after inheritance
rows.note: No official source publishes a rent for a specific single-family home. This is the single largest uncertainty in the rent-versus-sell comparison and it drives the answer. Obtain a broker opinion of rent before deciding.

rows.label: Property tax pass-through to residential tenants
rows.value: San Francisco Administrative Code Chapter 37 establishes pass-through rates per $100 of assessed value set annually by the Board of Supervisors
rows.source_name: City and County of San Francisco Board of Supervisors, Resolution No. 447-25
rows.note: The resolution sets pass-through rates per $100 of assessed value by tenancy commencement date: $0.0008 for 2022-07-01 to 2023-06-30, $0.0015 for 2023-07-01 to 2024-06-30, and $0.0051 for 2024-07-01 to 2025-06-30. The rate for 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30 appears in the resolution but was not legible in the retrieved text.

rows.label: Current property tax as a share of current gross rent
rows.note: Left blank on purpose. It would be computed from the owner's tax figure (2,439 USD/yr) and rent (85,800 USD/yr), but the tax figure itself is flagged as inconsistent with San Francisco's official rate, so publishing a derived ratio would compound the error. Resolve the flag on the Flagged for Review page first.
